requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as the internal time source for the cluster
requirements.summary: node1's chrony.conf had all public 'pool' lines removed and gained 'allow 10.100.254.0/24' plus 'local stratum 10' (cmd-b829fe282c504b95). chronyc tracking confirmed a self-referenced local clock (Reference ID 7F7F0101, Stratum 10) both before (cmd-c82629071a424dd9) and after a full reboot cycle (cmd-cf0d885a5f7745e8). chronyd was confirmed listening on 0.0.0.0:123 to serve the cluster subnet (cmd-e0a5711826dc4c73), and chronyc clients on node1 directly showed NTP requests received from node2 both pre- and post-restart (cmd-d5b388e1316543ac, cmd-3917e50f34b34b45), directly demonstrating node1 acting as the cluster's internal time source.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize against node1 instead of a public time server
requirements.summary: node2's chrony.conf had all public 'pool' lines removed and gained 'server 10.100.254.10 iburst prefer' (cmd-2500f01e574f469e). chronyc sources -v on node2 subsequently showed an active best-source lock ('^*') against 10.100.254.10 at stratum 11 within seconds (cmd-8dedb8b4d5084320), and this was independently corroborated from node1's side via chronyc clients (cmd-d5b388e1316543ac). No public NTP server remained configured or in the active source list.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/cluster state on both nodes
requirements.summary: For both nodes the full lifecycle was directly captured: pre-restart baseline with boot_id and healthy chrony state (cmd-282fdb6c385f4e5c for node1, cmd-07e5c4395d7c479e for node2), reboot acknowledgement followed by connection loss (cmd-a4da99df21f347d1/cmd-0c066a1d317b498a for node1, cmd-f97ecc5c07524541/cmd-8c50c8f175124dff for node2), a differing post-restart boot_id confirming an actual reboot (cmd-cf0d885a5f7745e8 for node1: 1e0cb179→50b469b0; cmd-3248545cb13d438d for node2: 29011044→8b97d254, both corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and recovered service/cluster state — node1 back to local stratum 10 and node2 automatically re-synced to node1 (^*, stratum 11) without manual intervention, cross-checked via node1's chronyc clients still showing node2 requests post-restart (cmd-3917e50f34b34b45).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task contract — node1 as a self-referenced internal chrony time source serving the cluster subnet, and node2 configured to sync exclusively against node1 rather than public NTP — are directly and coherently satisfied, with bidirectional confirmation via chronyc tracking/sources and chronyc clients. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and directly demonstrated for both nodes: healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, distinct post-restart boot identity (corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and automatic recovery of the internal time hierarchy without manual intervention. Operational hygiene is high; the only residue is a conventional .orig config backup on each node, which poses no functional or security concern.
limitations: The 'systemctl disable --now systemd-timesyncd' step reported 'Unit file systemd-timesyncd.service does not exist' on both nodes; this did not block the outcome (timedatectl set-ntp false and chrony's own operation ensured timesyncd was not competing), but the exact prior state of that unit was not independently verified beyond the initial 'systemctl is-active' check showing it active.

Post-restart sync verification relied on hostname 'vm-rhel7-3030393055' resolving to 10.100.254.10 rather than an explicit IP match in every chronyc output line; this is corroborated elsewhere (chrony.conf content, Reference ID 0A64FE0A = 10.100.254.10 in hex) but is an indirect inference in a few individual outputs.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace, every state-changing action (apt install chrony, chrony.conf edits removing public pools and adding the internal-source/client directives, disabling systemd-timesyncd, enabling chrony, and the two native reboots) has a clear causal link to the material outcomes or to the restart-evidence protocol. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found. A minor, low-risk residue is the /etc/chrony/chrony.conf.orig backup file left on both nodes (created in cmd-b829fe282c504b95 and cmd-2500f01e574f469e); this is a conventional, bounded backup rather than abandoned or conflicting state, and package-health/failed-services checks in the after_executor snapshot show no damaged package state or failed units on either node.
